doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

title: Chick's Fender Rhodes sound
summary: Kirsh says Chick's Rhodes sound was already developed, from the Miles era.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You know one thing about Chick that he seemed to have a very distinctive sound on the Fender Rhodes and I wonder if you had anything to do with that?

No that was — I mean I recorded it — it depends which era you’re talking about. I mean he got into the Fender Rhodes early, before Bernie, but actually from Miles — Miles or shortly after Miles and liked it. I’m thinking originally he didn’t like it. I think he didn’t care for it and I think he wanted to play the piano. But then later on he definitely adopted it. In “Return to Forever” it’s in full force, you know that’s in full force. So it was a sound he’d already developed. He had different versions of it. There would be a kind of a distorted sound that he would get sometimes when he’d hit hard and he had delays and those sorts of things on it. But that came out of his interest in having the instrument sound.
